coverage_notes:
Read: all of ledger-walls.txt, corrected.md (79 round-1 items), and the terrain/grass/aniso entries in ledger-open and ledger-compact. In code I read the whole assembled terrain fragment monolith (terrain.js 1684-4073), its spliced modules (terrain_micro, terrain_far_simplify, terrain_round, terrain_water_flow, vfx/fx_lights), the batched-GLSL rewrite (terrain_batch.js 190-355, 600-650), three r184 BatchedMesh.onBeforeRender, far_terrain.js, visual_ground.js, terrain_grass.js, terrain_rock.js, the punch/terrainLast sort (atmosphere_pipeline.js 775-837, draw_sort_program.js, index.js 1737-1760), the anisotropy plumbing (terrain_bc7.js 190-251/1295-1415, adapter.js 1557-1612, terrain.js 4700-4806) and the 10-17 census files in /mnt/wbterminal1/tmp/fps-agent (gpucensus2.json, terrmat.json, terrab.js).

Facts established:
(1) Draws. Terrain is one BatchedMesh with about 48 visible landblock ranges (ANGLE emulates one draw per range). There are about 11 far-ring patches (0.16 ms), 4 grass ring draws (0.51 ms), and one draw each for pebbles and grit.
(2) Ring overlap is small:
- Far patches discard inside the near ring (far_terrain.js:500-507). They draw before the near ring (renderOrder -1), but only near-horizon pixels are involved.
- visual_ground.js draws nothing (it is a render-only z offset).
- Grass and pebbles hang off worldRoot (phase 2), so under terrainLast they already draw before terrain and act as occluders. I checked and dropped the idea of reordering them.
(3) Texture taps per pixel at ultra:
- Near pixel in a transition cell: 4 texelFetch on uVertexTypes (plus 3 per-LB gate fetches in the batch) and 6 texelFetch on uMergeData.
- POM: 1-8 BC7 textureGrad taps under 25 m.
- TexMerge: base albedo, base 1x1-mip mean and base nra. Each overlay adds a mask (RGBA8, aniso 16), height-blend height taps that duplicate the albedo taps, the overlay albedo, a 1x1-mip mean and an nra tap.
- Detail texture: 1 tap under 50 m. Micro relief: 2-6 detail-normal taps (RGBA8) under 75 m. Bevel: up to 16 texelFetch on the ~50% of pixels within 2 m of a retail edge. Cloud shadow: 1 tap.
- Macro: 2 taps past 55 m. Far harmonize: 4 1x1-mip taps past 120 m.
- Totals: about 12-20 filtered taps for a near transition pixel, about 7-14 for a uniform cell. A far pixel past 300 m gets about 11 (bilinear fallback).
(4) Triplanar exists only in the Gouraud-off detail-normal block. That block is dead in every default session: roundMinLevel 2 subdivides every landblock (terrain.js:5743-5781), so every landblock sets the Gouraud bit (terrain_batch.js:332-336).
(5) terrainFarSimplify fades TexMerge over 240-300 m, the detail texture past 50 m and the Gouraud-off normals. POM, micro relief and height blend already stop by 25/75/90 m. The bevel, the cloud-shadow tap and the FX-light loop run at every distance, but on flat ground only 5-8% of ground rows lie past 75 m and about 2-4% between 120 and 300 m (geometry probe at camera height 3-6 m, 60 deg vertical FOV). So per-landblock baked splat textures at mid or far range cannot buy much: terrain cost is near-field.
(6) Vertices: 9 landblocks at 2048 triangles plus the rest at 512 gives about 40-60k triangles, which is not a lever.
(7) Anisotropy: the BC7 colour and nra arrays get 16 (one value for both channels, terrain_bc7.js:1410/1302). The detail-normal, detail-texture, mask and macro arrays get the preset 16.

Examined and NOT reported:
(a) FXC hoisting (X4121) of the remaining implicit-LOD texture() taps out of the distance gates (micro, detail texture, macro, road; in the batch also the Gouraud-off block, because acGouraud becomes a per-pixel texelFetch). The 10-17 A/B (uniform-gated procedural micro off: -1.1 ms) argues against full hoisting; FXC most likely emits sample_d with hoisted derivatives. A no-code 1070 check would settle it: `__terrainMicro.set({fadeStartM:0,fadeEndM:0.01})` against `{procedural:0}` on the terrain timer.
(b) Bevel fetch dedupe (16 to 9 texelFetch): about 0.05 ms.
(c) Grass vertex-shader early-outs: under 0.05 ms of ALU.
(d) terrainRock (open lead 149/246/647): an 18k-instance octahedron is about 432k vertex-shader invocations with a trivial fragment shader. Its GPU cost should be far below the 1.5 ms bar; the CPU scatter side was not examined.
(e) Define-gating the dead Gouraud-off lighting path (detail-normal, PBR, env and slope blocks) in the batch would extend gpu-shading-6. It is pixel-identical but probably 0-0.1 ms; fxc dcl_temps should gate it.
(f) Water ripple hash sharing: under 0.05 ms.

Gain basis for all three findings: the 10-17 per-feature A/Bs (texture merge -1.5, detail normal -1.1, detail texture -0.4, macro -0.3, POM -0.27 ms, recorded at terrain_far_simplify.js:8-10). Those ran with log depth and CSM on, so scale them down for terrainLast towns. Nothing was measured this session.

The angle is now largely exhausted for pixel-identical wins. The remaining big terrain items (the TexMerge and micro features themselves) are look features, and they can only be cut with an eye test.

findings.title: The terrain BatchedMesh draws its ~48 landblock ranges in slot order, not front-to-back, so terrain hidden behind nearer hills is fully shaded; turn on three's built-in opaque sort
findings.evidence:
What the code does:
- terrain_batch.js:608-612 sets `bm.sortObjects = false` (comment: 'OPAQUE terrain: skip the per-frame instance depth sort') and `perObjectFrustumCulled = true`.
- In three r184 (node_modules/three/src/objects/BatchedMesh.js), the unsorted branch already walks every instance each frame, tests its bounding sphere and rewrites multiDrawStarts/Counts and the indirect array. :1668 sets `indirectTexture.needsUpdate = true` every frame either way. The sorted branch (:1570-1613) only adds a z push and `list.sort(sortOpaque)`, which is front-to-back.

Why order matters:
- Draw order follows instance ids. Ids are recycled by park/steal/re-absorb (terrain_batch.js header lines 46-90). The LOD re-bake (terrain.js:5760-5781, F12-6) evicts and re-absorbs exactly the nearest landblocks as the player moves. So the nearest landblocks, the main terrain occluders, can land anywhere in the order.
- Early-Z is live for terrain under the reversed-Z default: gl_FragDepth is written only under log depth (terrain.js:2282/2526-2531) and there is no discard in the program.
- terrainLast (atmosphere_pipeline.js:792-816) already puts every other occluder first. Terrain-on-terrain overdraw is the remaining case, and unsorted ranges leave it on the table.
- 10-17 census: terrain-batch-x 6.17 ms, multiDrawCount 48 (gpucensus2.json, terrmat.json).

Rider: far patches use renderOrder -1 ('draw before the near ring: cheap early-z for it', far_terrain.js:1595). They lie behind the near ring and discard any overlap (:500-507), so that order is back-to-front and gives the near ring no early-Z.
findings.proposal:
Set `bm.sortObjects = true` on the terrain batch; three's default sortOpaque by bounding-sphere view z is enough. A distance-to-landblock-AABB `customSort` is an optional refinement. Ship it default-on with a `?terrainBatchSort=off` escape.

Pixel identity: draws are opaque and depth-resolved, and landblock meshes do not overlap, so only exact-depth ties at landblock seams could flip, and both sides draw the same ground.

Rider (optional): give the far patches renderOrder +1 so near hills early-reject far-patch fragments and the far shader's discard work. It stays order-independent because of farDepthBias and the discard.

Note for gl-driver-2: its span-merging half would then coalesce only rows adjacent in sorted order. Its no-gl_DrawID half is unaffected.
findings.expected_gain:
About 0.05-0.5 ms GPU at ultra, scene-dependent and unmeasured:
- Roughly 0 on flat ground (a heightfield seen from above does not self-occlude).
- About 3-10% of the terrain draw where near ridges or hillsides hide farther ground; much of Dereth's ring is hilly.
- Hidden fragments are mostly mid-range (TexMerge, macro, harmonize), cheaper than near-field ones.
- Cost: sorting about 48 entries on the CPU, roughly 5-10 us per frame. No GL work is added, since the indirect texture is already uploaded every frame.
- The far-ring rider is at most 0.05 ms (that ring costs 0.16 ms in total).
findings.novelty_check: rg over ledger-walls, ledger-compact, ledger-open and corrected.md for sortObjects, front-to-back, self-occlusion, instance order and terrain order. The only hits are depthBandSort and ledger-open:236, which concern the scene-level opaque sort between render items, never the ordering inside the terrain BatchedMesh. The git log shows `bm.sortObjects = false` unchanged since 61afddd1.

findings.title: TexMerge and POM fetch the same BC7 atlas texel twice; also skip harmonize-only and splat-noise work where its result is unused
findings.area: scene3d/terrain.js main() TexMerge and POM; scene3d/terrain_micro.js height blend
findings.evidence:
(a) Height blend:
- The base albedo tap uses `terrainAtlasTex(clamp(baseLayer), isWaterCode(baseLayer) ? waterCellUv : cellUv)` (terrain.js:2893-2894). Each overlay tap uses the same select form (:2981-2982).
- The height-blend splice that follows re-fetches both through `terrainHbHeight(code, cellUv)` = `terrainAtlasTex(c, cellUv).a - terrainTypeMeanTex(c).a` (terrain_micro.js:591-594, slot splice :620-626, `if (!hbHSet) hbH = terrainHbHeight(baseLayer, cellUv)`).
- That splice runs only when `!isWaterCode(layer) && !isWaterCode(baseLayer)`, so it reads the same layer, uv and gradients: the same texel.
- A compiler cannot CSE these: the first tap's uv is a select and the second's is plain cellUv inside a branch. Removing the duplicate needs path-sensitive select folding.
- Active on transition cells within 90 m (uHeightBlendFade 30-90; uPbrEnabled=1 per terrmat.json).

(b) POM:
- The loop samples `terrainAtlasTex(pomCode, cellUv + uvOff).a` in a loop-local (terrain.js:2650-2659), then does `cellUv += uvOff` (:2660).
- On a hit (break), that last sample is exactly the texel the base albedo tap re-fetches whenever pomCode == baseLayer, which holds for every uniform non-road cell.
- POM covers about 80% of ground rows (depression above 8.6 deg and nearer than 25 m at a 3-4 m camera).

(c) Unused work:
- mergedMean is accumulated with 1x1-mip taps for the base and every slot (:2895, :2984), but it is read only by far harmonize, which needs depth > uFarHarmonizeStart = 120 m (:3009-3011).
- splatN (two value noises, 8 sin hashes, :2909-2934) is computed for every merge pixel, even cells with no valid overlay, the only consumer.
findings.proposal:
Bit-identical rewrites:
- (a) Fetch each slot texel once as a vec4 (`ovTex`, `baseTex`). Use `.rgb` for albedo. Inside the height-blend block use `.a - terrainTypeMeanTex(c).a`: that block only runs when the layer is not water, so the uv is identical.
- (b) Keep the POM hit sample as a vec4 with its code. In the base slot reuse its `.rgb` when the loop broke, pomCode == baseLayer, the base is not water, and no snow or mud dent has moved cellUv since (those families are default-off).
- (c) Gate the mergedMean accumulation on `uFarHarmonize > 0 && vViewDepth > uFarHarmonizeStart`, and compute splatN lazily at the first valid overlay.

Ship it default-on with an `=off` escape that assembles today's program character-for-character, like terrainFarSimplify.
findings.expected_gain:
About 0.1-0.2 ms GPU near-field at ultra (derived, unmeasured), and 0 if the driver already folds the duplicates.
- Per-tap cost basis: the POM A/B (-0.27 ms for about 2-4 BC7 steps on about 80% of terrain pixels) implies roughly 0.1 ms per BC7 tap per terrain pixel.
- (b) removes about 1 tap on about 70% of terrain pixels.
- (a) removes 1 + n taps on transition pixels (about 40% of cells, assumed).
- (c) is ALU and 1x1-mip taps, about 0.02-0.05 ms.
findings.novelty_check: rg for height blend, hbHeight, duplicate or redundant tap, same texel, mergedMean, harmSharp and splat noise across ledgers and corrected.md: no hits. Round-1 gpu-shading-6 was about define-gating dead family blocks, not tap dedupe. terrainFarSimplify (b249a762) removed only the dead bilinear taps.
findings.verify_how:
- Node test on `_terrainGlslForTest()`: assert one atlas tap per slot and no `terrainHbHeight(` call on a slot already fetched.
- Bit identity: readPixels diff at a frozen pose on laptop SwiftShader, transition cells under 25 m in view.
- Gain: terrain-batch-x timer ABAB on the 1070 via the escape flag (needs a reload per arm, since the program is session-constant).

findings.title: The micro-relief detail-normal array, the costliest terrain texture per tap, is uncompressed RGBA8 although the default path reads only .rg; repack to RG8 (pixel-identical), with BC5 or a fade-band anisotropy cap as eye-tested follow-ons
findings.area: scene3d/adapter.js loadTerrainDetailNormalArray; scene3d/terrain_micro.js terrainMicroSlice; mask array in scene3d/terrain.js
findings.evidence:
The texture and who reads it:
- adapter.js:1557-1612 builds `scene3d-terrain-detail-normal-array`: 5 slices x 1024^2, RGBA8 (4 B/texel), trilinear, `anisotropy = _maxAnisotropy` (16 at ultra, quality.js:532).
- On the default path its only reader is micro relief: terrainMicroSlice (terrain_micro.js:470-479) does two taps per slice, reading `.rg` only. Up to 3 slices (6 taps) run under 75 m (:525-585), typically 2-3 taps.
- The only reader of `.b` is the Gouraud-off detail-normal block (terrain.js:3346-3405, `!acGouraud`). It is dead by default: every landblock is subdivided at roundMinLevel 2 (terrain.js:5743-5781), so the per-landblock Gouraud bit is 1 everywhere (terrain_batch.js:332-336). The far bake skips the block (fsKeep 0 at 1000 m), and its output is albedo-only anyway.

Cost evidence:
- 10-17 A/B: detail normal off = -1.1 ms for about 2.5 taps per near pixel (terrain_far_simplify.js:8-10).
- The same census implies about 0.1 ms per BC7 (1 B/texel) atlas tap per pixel (POM -0.27 ms for several steps on about 80% of pixels).
- So each detail-normal tap costs about 3-4x a BC7 tap. That fits bandwidth/cache-bound minified anisotropic sampling of a 4 B/texel array.

Same pattern, lower stakes: the TexMerge mask array is RGBA8 (terrain.js:4775-4806) but read only as `.r` (:2967-2968).
findings.proposal:
1. Pixel-identical on every default path: after the PNG decode in loadTerrainDetailNormalArray, repack to an RG8 DataArrayTexture (THREE.RGFormat; same filters, mips and anisotropy), halving bytes per tap.
   - Keep RGBA8 when the session can light a landblock through the Gouraud-off path (?terrainGouraud=off, or terrainRound off with landblocks below subdiv 2). Alternatively reconstruct z there.
   - Optionally repack the mask array to R8 the same way.
2. Follow-ons, default-off and needs-eyetest:
   - (a) BC5/RGTC2 (EXT_texture_compression_rgtc is exposed on ANGLE D3D11) with JS- or offline-built mips: 1 B/texel, the BC7 atlas byte rate.
   - (b) An anisotropy budget for the non-albedo arrays: detail normal, the BC7 nra (it only feeds micro relief by default), detail texture and macro. Cap at 4, or clamp the ratio in-shader via textureGrad only inside the 20-75 m micro fade band, so near ground keeps 16.
   - The albedo atlas keeps its terrainAniso 16 floor.
findings.expected_gain:
- RG8: 0.2-0.5 ms GPU at ultra if the taps are bandwidth/cache-bound as the per-tap ratio suggests (half the bytes of a 1.1 ms feature); about 0 if they are filter-rate-bound. Unmeasured.
- BC5: up to about 0.6-0.8 ms.
- Anisotropy cap: about 30% fewer probes on these taps at a 3 m camera. 12-75 m holds 28-41% of ground rows, with a mean anisotropy ratio of 4.5-8.4 (geometry probe). That gives about 0.15-0.4 ms.
- The mask R8 repack is likely small (the masks are cache-resident).
findings.novelty_check: rg for aniso across ledgers: only terrainAniso (the albedo floor), the refuted 08-05 'aniso16 stack slowdown' (measured while CPU-bound, so it does not bind on today's fill-bound towns), and atlas-statics mip/aniso leads. Nothing on the detail-normal array format, RG8/BC5, or anisotropy of the non-albedo terrain arrays. The texture-pipeline owner decisions (Remacri, XUBC7) concern albedo only.
findings.verify_how:
No code needed for the A/B on the 1070:
- In the console, build an RG8 DataArrayTexture from `uTerrainDetailNormalArray.value.image.data` (copy bytes 0-1 of every 4; generateMipmaps; anisotropy 16) and swap it into terrain-batch-x's uniform. Same sampler type, so no recompile.
- Read the terrain draw timer ABAB with the terrab.js harness; readPixels diff at a frozen pose for identity (at most 1 LSB if the driver's mip generator rounds differently by format).

Anisotropy follow-on: poke TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT=4 directly via gl.texParameterf on the bound GL textures. Never set needsUpdate on the BC7 arrays: their CPU mirrors are freed. Then eye-test grazing ground at 10-75 m in grassland and rock.

verdicts.code_truth:
The mechanism is real. I checked each cited line at HEAD:
- terrain_batch.js:610-611: `bm.sortObjects = false; bm.perObjectFrustumCulled = true;`.
- three 0.184.0 BatchedMesh.js:1522 early-outs only when `!perObjectFrustumCulled && !sortObjects`, so terrain already walks and culls every instance each frame.
- The sorted branch (:1570-1613) adds only the z dot, the `_renderList.push` and `list.sort(sortOpaque)`. sortOpaque (:21-25) is `a.z - b.z`, front-to-back.
- The vertex rewrite reads `getBatchingMatrix(getIndirectIndex(gl_DrawID))` (terrain_batch.js:222), and per-LB data comes from the aLbSlot attribute. Reordering the ranges is therefore safe.
- addInstance (:580-586) reuses the lowest freed id, so draw order is whatever park, steal and re-absorb leave behind.
- Under reversed-Z the terrain writes no gl_FragDepth (terrain.js:2526-2531 is inside `#if USE_LOGARITHMIC_DEPTH_BUFFER`), and none of the terrain modules contains a discard.
- far_terrain.js:1595 has `renderOrder = -1 // draw before the near ring: cheap early-z for it`, which is backwards: the far geometry lies behind the near ring. The discard at :500-507 is confirmed, and the reversed-Z path never writes gl_FragDepth (:416-441).

One claim is false. The finding says no GL work is added because 'the indirect texture is already uploaded every frame'. At HEAD, `?bmIndirectPerCamera` (default ON) patches BatchedMesh.prototype.onBeforeRender (batched_indirect_per_camera.js:164-232). It applies to terrain because perObjectFrustumCulled is true, and it rolls back the version bump whenever the culled id prefix is unchanged, so a still or straight-walking camera uploads nothing. With sorting on, the prefix changes whenever the depth order of the visible landblocks changes, which happens while turning or moving and on near-tie flip-flops.

A smaller error: the LOD re-bake re-absorb takes the lowest free id, which often puts near landblocks early. The current order is arbitrary, not systematically bad.
verdicts.novelty: New. In ledger-compact, ledger-open and corrected.md, sortObjects appears only for static or pool buckets (compact 716, 808; open 232), and depthBandSort / open-236 concern the scene-level opaque sort. git log -S shows `bm.sortObjects = false` unchanged since 61afddd1. url-flags has no terrain-batch sort row. Interplay: gl-driver-2's span merging would only coalesce rows that are adjacent after sorting.
verdicts.wall_conflict:
No wall conflict:
- Wall 113 (perObjectFrustumCulled must stay on) is respected.
- Ledger-compact 716 ('early-out also needs !sortObjects') does not apply, because culling already defeats the early-out.
- Walls 105/141 (CPU-bound frame) are superseded for fill-bound ultra towns per the 10-19 picture.
- Wall 81 (8.33 ms grid) means a gain this small will not show as fps.
verdicts.visual_safety:
Pixel-identical in practice:
- Draws are opaque and depth-resolved.
- Shared landblock edges have bit-identical world positions (exact 192 m translations, same land heights), so seams are watertight and have no double-covered pixels where order could matter.
- LOD T-junctions produce cracks, not overlaps.
- Far-ring rider: farDepthBias pushes far terrain behind the near ring, so there are no ties under GEQUAL, and the discard keeps it order-independent.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Overstated:
- Terrain-on-terrain overlap from a 3-6 m camera is mostly a thin band below each ridge silhouette: hidden far ground compresses toward the horizon.
- Hiding inside one 192 m landblock (hill and valley in the same landblock) follows index order and is not helped by sorting landblocks.
- The hidden fragments are mid or far range, where POM, micro relief, height blend and part of the detail texture work are already off.
- Towns, where the 50 fps limit is, are flat, and terrainLast already handles the building occluders, so the gain there is about 0.
- Corrected: about 0 in towns, roughly 0.02-0.15 ms GPU in hilly vistas, unmeasured.
- Costs: CPU sort about 5-10 us, plus up to one extra ~1 KB indirect texSubImage2D per frame while turning (about 10-30 us across the renderer and CrGpuMain), where today that upload is often skipped.
- Far-ring rider: at most 0.05 ms of its 0.16 ms.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
Setting sortObjects=true on terrain-batch-x (terrain_batch.js:610) is safe and pixel-identical. It makes the ~48 landblock ranges draw front-to-back, and three r184 already walks every instance because per-object culling is on. Ship behind a `?terrainBatchSort=off` escape; a distance-to-AABB customSort is better than sphere-centre z. Give the far patches (far_terrain.js:1595) renderOrder +1 so they draw after the near ring and early-reject behind near hills; that is also pixel-identical.

It is not free on the GL side: bmIndirectPerCamera (default ON) currently skips the indirect upload whenever the culled id list is unchanged, and sorting adds about one tiny upload per frame while the camera turns. Expected gain is about 0 in flat towns and about 0.02-0.15 ms GPU in hilly views, unmeasured. It is a cheap hygiene item, not an fps lever. Verify with the terrab.js per-draw timer at a ridge pose, toggling bm.sortObjects live.

verdicts.code_truth:
All three sub-claims hold at HEAD.

(a) Height-blend duplicates:
- The base tap is `terrainAtlasTex(clamp(baseLayer,0,32), isWaterCode(baseLayer) ? waterCellUv : cellUv)` (terrain.js:2893-2894). The overlay tap is the same select form (:2981-2982).
- The height-blend splice (terrain_micro.js:620-626) runs only under `!isWaterCode(layer) && !isWaterCode(baseLayer)` and calls terrainHbHeight(code, cellUv) = `terrainAtlasTex(c, cellUv).a - terrainTypeMeanTex(c).a` (:591-594).
- The gradUv default is ON (terrain_micro.js:254-255), so terrainAtlasTex is textureGrad with the global gTerrainGridDx/Dy (:394-417). Identical (code, cellUv) means an identical texel. No cellUv write sits between the taps; the only writes are at :2660, :2705 and :2755, all before the merge.
- The splice also re-fetches the 1x1-mip mean, terrainTypeMeanTex(c).a, which duplicates the mergedMean `terrainTypeMean()` .rgb taps (:2895, :2984). That is a free extension of (a).

(b) POM hit sample:
- On break the loop has not added the last step: `float mapH = terrainAtlasTex(pomCode, cellUv + uvOff).a; if (mapH >= layerH) break; ... uvOff += stepUv;` and then `cellUv += uvOff;` (:2655-2660). The hit sample is therefore exactly the base texel when pomCode == baseLayer.
- pack_merge_record (crates/holtburger-dat/src/terrain_merge.rs:434; test :713-715) makes slot 0 of a uniform cell its terrain code, and the atlas layer is the code. POM is skipped on water-touching cells (:2627).

(c) Unused work:
- harmSharpMean/mergedMean is read only in the harmonize block, behind `harmF = smoothstep(uFarHarmonizeStart, ...)` (:3009-3024; uFarHarmonizeStart 120 per terrmat.json).
- splatN (:2909-2934) is consumed only inside the overlay loop (:2975).
- Height blend is default-on at medium and above (hbAmount 1, fade 30-90). terrmat.json shows uPbrEnabled 1 and uPomFadeEnd 25.
verdicts.novelty: New. The ledgers and corrected.md have no hits for height blend, hbHeight, duplicate or same-texel taps, mergedMean or splat noise. gpu-shading-6 (define-gating dead family blocks) and terrainFarSimplify b249a762 (dead bilinear taps) are different items.
verdicts.wall_conflict: None. No new sampler (wall 191 respected). Same program key structure behind an escape flag. Walls 105/141 do not apply to fill-bound towns.
verdicts.visual_safety: Bit-identical on the default path (gradUv on): the same textureGrad arguments give the same vec4. With ?terrainGradUv=off the in-branch implicit-derivative taps already differ from the outside tap, so keep the legacy text under the escape, as proposed. The (c) gate at vViewDepth > uFarHarmonizeStart is exact, because smoothstep is 0 at or below the start.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Slightly overstated:
- Each removed tap re-reads a texel that is already in L1, so the saving is TMU issue and anisotropic filter work, not DRAM bandwidth.
- (b) saves one anisotropic BC7 tap on POM-hit uniform-cell pixels under ~23 m, about 0.03-0.08 ms.
- (a) saves about 1.3 taps on transition pixels under 90 m, about 0.03-0.06 ms.
- (c) is ALU plus cached 1x1-mip taps, about 0.01-0.03 ms.
- Risk for (b): holding a vec3 and a flag live from the POM march through the snow and mud blocks to the merge can raise the register count of an already huge shader and cost occupancy. Check fxc dcl_temps (or a register count on the 1070) before and after.
- The finder's 'compiler cannot CSE' is plausible for FXC, because the selects are path-sensitive, but unproven for NVIDIA's backend.
- Corrected total: about 0.05-0.12 ms GPU near-field at ultra, possibly about 0, unmeasured.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
These are exact rewrites of the terrain fragment shader, shipped default-on with an `=off` escape that keeps today's text:
- (a) Fetch each TexMerge slot's atlas texel once as a vec4, and reuse its .a in terrainHbHeight. That is valid because the height-blend block runs only for non-water layers, whose tap used cellUv. Also fetch each slot's 1x1-mip mean once, which serves both mergedMean .rgb and the height-blend .a.
- (b) Carry the POM hit texel (code plus vec4) out of the march, and reuse its .rgb for the base albedo when the loop broke and pomCode == clamp(baseLayer). The snow and mud dents are default-off, but gate on them too.
- (c) Accumulate mergedMean only when uFarHarmonize > 0 and vViewDepth > uFarHarmonizeStart, and compute splatN at the first valid overlay.

The output is bit-identical with gradUv on. Gain: about 0.05-0.12 ms GPU, unmeasured. It is 0 if the driver already folds the duplicates, and it could go negative if (b) raises the register count.

Gates:
- A node test on _terrainGlslForTest() checking that there is one atlas tap per slot.

verdicts.code_truth:
The texture and its readers:
- adapter.js:1557-1612 builds `scene3d-terrain-detail-normal-array` as RGBA8 (`tex.format = T.RGBAFormat`), with trilinear filtering, mips and `anisotropy = _maxAnisotropy`. quality.js ultra sets `anisotropy: 16`.
- The assets are five 1024x1024 RGB PNGs (scene3d/assets/terrain_detail/*.png), decoded to RGBA through a canvas.
- Default reader: terrainMicroSlice (terrain_micro.js:470-479), two implicit-derivative texture() taps reading `.rg`. They sit inside `if (uMicroAmt.z > 0.0 && uDetailNormalEnabled > 0.5)` (:536). That explains the 10-17 terrab.js A/B: toggling uDetailNormalEnabled took off the procedural micro relief, -1.1 ms.
- The only reader of `.rgb` is the Gouraud-off block, `if (uDetailNormalEnabled > 0.5 && !acGouraud)` (terrain.js:3346-3405).

Why that block is dead by default:
- The finder's reason is wrong: terrainRound minLevel defaults to 1 (terrain_round.js:106, :175-179, :218-219). The terrain.js:5774 '2 by default' comment is stale.
- The real reason: canSubdivide routes even level-1 landblocks through fetch_subdivided_landblock (terrain.js:4350-4356, 6105-6142), and subdividedLandblockMeshToGeometry supplies acLightNormal (adapter.js:383-387). With terrainGouraud ON (terrain.js:1080-1088), every landblock's batch A-bit is 1 (terrain_batch.js:332-336).
- That bit is per landblock and decided at runtime. If the subdivide fetch throws (terrain.js:6111-6116), the landblock falls back to landblockMeshToGeometry with no acLightNormal and is lit through the Gouraud-off block, which reads .b. A session-level 'keep RGBA8' rule therefore cannot cover it.

Other checks:
- far_terrain.js does not sample the array (its block uses a flat normal, :527-529).
- The far bake skips the block because of fsKeep (terrain_far_simplify.js:250).
- The mask array is RGBA8 and read only as .r (terrain.js:4775-4806, 2968), but it is 8 masks at 256x256 and cache-resident.
verdicts.novelty: New. ledger-open 282/349 (NRA to BC5/BC7 bake) concerns the static NRA arrays, not this 5-slice terrain detail-normal array. Wall 120 (context-loss restore re-uploads from image.data): keep the RG8 bytes as image.data, and the restore stays intact.

One mandatory change: because the per-LB Gouraud-off fallback is a runtime event, the Gouraud-off block must reconstruct z from .rg, not read .b. Only those rare fallback landblocks, and ?terrainGouraud=off sessions, would then differ, at the 1-LSB-normal level. The anisotropy-cap and BC5 follow-ons change pixels: they are quality trades and must stay default-off behind an eye test.
verdicts.gain_realism:
Uncertain and probably small:
- The 3-4x per-tap ratio is not clean evidence of bandwidth-bound taps. The -1.1 ms also removed the slice-selection ALU, and these taps are heavily minified (427 texels/m at the 2.4 m fine tile, versus the atlas being near-magnified up close), so anisotropic probe count (TMU rate, format-independent for 8-bit formats) is at least as likely a driver.
- RG8 halves the L1/L2 footprint and the DRAM traffic, but it does not reduce probes.
- Corrected: RG8 about 0.05-0.25 ms GPU at ultra, unmeasured. Certain side benefit: about 13 MB less VRAM, mips included.
- BC5: about the same plus a little more, at M effort.
- Anisotropy cap: possibly 0.1-0.4 ms, but it is a look trade.
- Mask R8: about 0.
verdicts.corrected_claim:
Repacking the terrain detail-normal array (adapter.js:1557-1612) from RGBA8 to RG8 (THREE.RGFormat; same filters, mips and anisotropy 16) is pixel-identical on the default path, where only terrainMicroSlice's `.rg` taps read it. It halves bytes and cache footprint per tap and saves about 13 MB of VRAM.

The Gouraud-off detail-normal block (terrain.js:3377-3396) must reconstruct z from .rg. Its trigger is not session-constant: a landblock whose subdivided fetch fails falls back per landblock to the non-Gouraud path (terrain.js:6111-6116 together with terrain_batch.js:332-336). The dead block is not caused by roundMinLevel 2, which defaults to 1. It is dead because every level≥1 landblock goes through subdividedLandblockMeshToGeometry, which carries acLightNormal.

Expected gain is about 0.05-0.25 ms GPU, unmeasured, and lower if the taps are bound by anisotropic probe rate. Test it first with the console RG8 swap and the terrab.js timer on the 1070. BC5 and a reduced anisotropy for the non-albedo terrain arrays are separate, default-off, eye-tested look trades. The mask R8 repack is negligible.

findings.title: Pool light loop: skip lights out of range with an exact squared-range test before getPointLightInfo / getSpotLightInfo
findings.area: scene3d/light_loops.js (lights_fragment_begin plain loops): all lit MeshStandard/Lambert draws (statics, building shells, cell statics, entities, grass)
findings.evidence:
**What runs today**
- `light_loops.js:43-56` and `:76-79`: the plain loop runs `pointLight = pointLights[i]; getPointLightInfo(...)` for all 16 point slots and both spot slots.
- Only `RE_Direct` is skipped, via `if (directLight.visible)`.
- three `lights_pars_begin.glsl.js:111-122`: `getPointLightInfo` always runs normalize + length + `getDistanceAttenuation` before visibility is known.
  - The stock law (`:56-68`) uses pow, rcp, a pow4 window and pow2. Building floor-bias, cell-baked and cell-static clones run it, because clone() dropped the clamp patch.
  - The lightClamp base materials (`materials.js:2761-2770`) use linear `saturate(1 - d/c)`.

**Why almost every slot is out of range**
- Pool: 16 point + 2 spot (`lighting.js:630-631`).
- Active slots are a prefix. The tail is parked at y = -1e5 with distance 1 m (`lighting.js:1003-1018`, `:1048-1049`, `:1150-1156`).
- Every DAT falloff is 1..15 m, times 1.3 (`lighting.js:3644-3649`). So ranges are 1.3-19.5 m.
- The 2 spot slots are essentially always parked (`lighting.js:604`: spots are "~absent" in the DAT).

**Precedents and reach**
- Terrain's own pool loop already early-outs on range (`vfx/fx_lights.js:85`, `:88`).
- MeshLambert grass (`terrain_grass.js:902`, about 120k blades at ultra) runs the same chunk.

**Exactness probe** (float32, agent-scratch/range_skip_probe.mjs)
- 4M samples within ±1e-5 of the light sphere, 1.8M of them skipped.
- 0 skipped samples would have contributed light, under both the linear and the stock law, even with ±4 ulp sqrt/div error, using margin 1.000002.
findings.proposal:
**Shader change.** In `patchLightLoopsChunk`'s plain body, insert the test between `pointLight = pointLights[ i ];` and the info call:

`vec3 hbL = pointLight.position - geometryPosition; if ( !( pointLight.distance > 0.0 && dot( hbL, hbL ) > pointLight.distance * pointLight.distance * 1.000002 ) ) { getPointLightInfo( ... ); if ( directLight.visible ) { RE_Direct(...) } }`

Do the same in the spot loop with `spotLight`.
- Nested-if form, so no `continue` is added and ANGLE's loop translation is unchanged.
- The `RE_Direct` call text stays byte-identical, so the lightClamp split/join still wraps it.
- The `distance > 0` guard keeps infinite-reach lights on the stock path.
- A NaN position fails the test and falls through to the stock path.

**Escape.** Boot-time `?lightRangeSkip=off`, read in `installLightLoops` before any program compiles, so no relink.

**Optional follow-on.** Put an active-slot count into the point-light UBO (lightUbo path) so idle slots cost zero instead of about 12 ops each. Only worth it if `__diag.lights` shows many idle slots in towns.

**Why not a per-object mask.** Building batches are per (landblock, material) (`buildings.js:168-176`) and statics sit in region buckets. A per-draw mask would be landblock-granular and would cost per-draw CPU on a main thread that is 98% busy. The per-pixel test culls at fragment granularity for about 13 ops per slot and no CPU.
findings.expected_gain:
**Per fragment (hand count):**
- Each out-of-range or parked slot drops from about 22 ALU + 2 transcendentals + 3 cbuffer loads (linear law) to about 13 ALU. Under the stock law it drops from about 30 ALU + 5 transcendentals.
- Over 18 slots that is roughly 200-300 issue slots out of an estimated 800-1000 per lit MeshStandard fragment, about 25%.
- About 35-45% for Lambert grass, whose BRDF is trivial.

**Per frame:** the lit world passes were 6-8 ms GPU in the 10-17 Holtburg census (log depth): statics 4.4, cells 1.6, grass 0.5, buildings 0.4, entities 0.3. Linvak buildings were 6.3 ms. I estimate 0.3-1.2 ms GPU per frame in towns at ultra, more at Linvak.

This is unmeasured, and only the ALU-limited share converts. It reaches fps only on GPU-bound frames (120 Hz grid caveat).

findings.area: scene3d/materials.js applyBakedVertexLightPatch / getCachedCellBaked (every baked EnvCell wall, floor and ceiling: dungeons, building interiors, outdoor-visible rooms)
findings.evidence:
**The default arm suppresses direct light**

- `applyBakedVertexLightPatch` (`:912-1004`) sets uniform `uAcBakedSuppressDirect = 1.0` (`:921`).

- So three's full direct pipeline runs first and is discarded.

**What runs and gets thrown away**
- Both directional `RE_Direct` calls (sun + legacy sun), unrolled.
- 16 point and 2 spot info evaluations, under the stock pow attenuation because the clone lost the clamp (gpu-shading-2).
- `RE_Direct` for every torch in range.

- `suppressDirect` is a session constant and the key already carries `|k`, so no new program-key bit is needed.
- Note in gpu-shading-2: re-installing the light clamp on cell-baked clones is pointless on the default arm.

findings.title: Zero-intensity scene lights are still shaded per pixel: the parked legacy sun (both suns indoors) and the zeroed SkyLightProbe SH

findings.evidence:
**Legacy sun**
- `index.js:6430-6431` zeroes it on the atmosphere path.
- `lighting.js:1588-1603` keeps it visible forever (light-count discipline) and zeroes it indoors.

**Takram sun:** goes to 0 indoors (`atmosphere_lights.js:109`, `:334-336`, `:356`).

**Directional loop**
- three `WebGLLights.js:277-281` uploads `color x intensity` with no skip.
- `lights_fragment_begin.glsl.js:132-150` calls `RE_Direct` unconditionally. `getDirectionalLightInfo` sets `visible = true`.
- lightLoops left this loop untouched (`light_loops.js` header).
- So every lit fragment pays a full GGX `RE_Direct`, plus the lightClamp wrapper on clamp materials, for a black light. Indoors it pays two.

- With IBL default-on (`ibl_environment.js:83-91`, `:251`), `skyProbe.intensity` is forced to 0 every tick (`atmosphere_lights.js:343`, `:360`): "Intensity 0, NEVER removal".
- three still counts the probe (`WebGLLights.js:268-276`), so `USE_LIGHT_PROBES` stays defined (`WebGLProgram.js:592`).

Extend the light_loops chunk patch. Both conditions read uniforms, so the branches are coherent across a warp.

**(a) Directional loop.** After the shadow `#if` block, wrap the call: `if ( any( notEqual( directLight.color, vec3( 0.0 ) ) ) ) { RE_Direct(...) }`. The call text is unchanged, so the clamp wrapper still applies. This is exact: zero colour gives zero irradiance, and through the clamp wrapper the delta is 0, `min(0, 0)` is 0, and the mix is 0.

**(b) Probe.** Wrap `irradiance += getLightProbeIrradiance( lightProbe, geometryNormal );` in `if ( any( notEqual( lightProbe[ 0 ], vec3( 0.0 ) ) ) )`. This is exact here: all 9 coefficients are scaled by the same intensity, and a positive sky irradiance has a positive DC term.

findings.title: Outdoor-visible interior cells are ordered against the building shells that enclose them only by program id: give cellsGroup an opaque sub-phase after the shells
findings.area: scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js _phaseOf / punchPhaseOpaqueSort + draw_sort_program.js (punchRetail single world pass)
findings.evidence:
**Shells and cells share one phase**
- punchRetail is default-on (`index.js:6281-6287`). Outdoors that makes one world pass ordered by phase (`atmosphere_pipeline.js:1457-1478`).
- `index.js:1752-1760` tags worldRoot = 2. Building shells, statics, cells and entities therefore all share phase 2.
- Both comparators then order by groupOrder, renderOrder, then program id (`draw_sort_program.js:80-94`; `atmosphere_pipeline.js:826-837`).
- No renderOrder is set on buildings or cells.

**The old guarantee was lost**
- Before punchRetail, the portalPunch split drew cells in a later pass, after the facade. Its design relies on "the building FACADE's own depth naturally masks the interior OUTSIDE the aperture" (`portal_punch.js:11-27`).
- In the single pass that masking saves shading only when the shell's program happens to have the lower id. That depends on compile order, which varies by boot and spot.
- Rooms that pass interiorApertureCull are drawn whole. Retail clips each room to its portal rect (`interior_aperture_cull.js:18-28`).
- Since reversedZ (10-19) early-Z makes this order cost GPU.

**Safe to reorder**
- Occlusion proxies draw last in the transparent list (`occlusion_cull.js:211`), so a reorder doesn't affect them.
- `__punchPhase` is read only by `_punchPhase` (`atmosphere_pipeline.js:778-790`).

**Cost:** census cells group 1.58-1.91 ms (cellstatic 1.0-1.3 + fused 0.56-0.62, log depth). The 0xE632 pagoda: 141 room draws, 1.6-1.9 ms.
findings.proposal:
**Change.**
- Tag `cellsGroup.userData.__punchPhase = 2.5`.
- In `_phaseOf`, return 2.5 only while `_cellsLastNow`, else 2.
- Set `_cellsLastNow` once per frame beside `_terrainLastNow` (`atmosphere_pipeline.js:2541`) as `!skyDome._lastIsIndoor && !indoorSplitArmed`. Indoors the cells should keep drawing first because they are the occluders.
- Opaque comparators only. The transparent sort is untouched (unlike `Group.renderOrder`, which would also reorder transparent blending).
- Escape `?cellsLast=off`.

**Why it is pixel-identical.**
- Opaque, depth-tested and depth-writing.
- Shells carry the floor bias (vertex z pulled toward the eye), so shell/cell coplanar contacts never tie.
- The only order-sensitive case left is an exact depth tie between an unbiased outdoor static and an EnvCell surface.
- At most one extra program switch at the sub-phase boundary.
findings.expected_gain:
**When it helps:** on frames where today's program order draws a cell program before the shells, the room's fragments outside the door or window (most of its projected area) are shaded and then overwritten. After the change, early-Z rejects them.

**Size:** estimated 0-0.6 ms GPU in town views with apertures in view, scaled from the cells-pass cost above. It is 0 where the accidental order is already favourable, and smaller once building-fill-2 cheapens cell shading.

**Side benefit:** removes a compile-order-dependent source of boot-to-boot GPU variance, which helps A/B hygiene (walls #116/#143).

findings.title: The static cache and mover scope never engage while the player moves or turns: every moving frame is FRUSTUM for all 3 cascades. Proposed fix: camera-centred, rotation-invariant cascades with per-cascade translation slack
findings.evidence:
Every moving frame refits all three cascades:
- csm.js:121-140: refit thresholds are 1 cm, 1e-3 rad of camera rotation and 1e-3 rad of sun.
- csm.js:500: any one exceeded means all three refit (513-524, didRefitThisTick=true at 548).
- The fit is the bounding sphere of the camera's view-depth slice (_fitCascade 710-720), so it depends on camera orientation (F1 note at 124-140).

That refit marks every cascade dirty and bypasses the cache:
- lighting.js:1730: refit sets shadowDirty.
- lighting.js:2351: fullMask = shadowDirty ? all : 0, so all three get the FRUSTUM reason.
- shadow_caster_list.js:608-610: FRUSTUM gives st.valid=false and NORMAL; at 625 all-NORMAL falls through to a plain full pass.
- The cache header says so itself: 'nothing is cached while the camera moves'.

So running, or any mouse-look over ~3°/s, re-rasters every cascade's statics every frame. That is exactly the ~12 ms/frame (+13 fps) the 10-17 moving measurement priced; the 10-17 caches (243a200f, da9f2dbf) do not touch it.

When idle:
- The sun alone crosses 1e-3 rad every ~1.2-2.5 s (derived from a ~7620 s AC day), producing a full 3-cascade NORMAL raster.
- The next mover frame then pays a second static raster as REFRESH, because NORMAL does not save the cache.
- The 10-17 idle bench logged 0 sun triggers in 180 frames, consistent with a pinned sky. Benches with a pinned sky never see this spike.
findings.proposal:
Make cascades independent of camera orientation and let them lag the camera within a slack zone.

(1) csm.js:
- Cascade i is a sphere of radius split_i + margin_i centred on a texel-snapped point in the existing world-anchored light frame.
- Refit cascade i only when the camera is more than margin_i from that centre, or the sun has stepped more than eps_i. Stagger sun refits so at most one cascade refits per frame, and allow c2 a 2e-3 rad threshold.
- Margins 5/10/28 m give exactly today's texel sizes at the default retail FOV (3.4 / 10.7 / 64 cm; computed with scratch csm_radii.mjs replicating _fitCascade).
- Recentres at 12 m/s run speed: every 0.42 / 0.83 / 2.3 s. Turning in place: never.
- Export csmState.refitMask.

(2) lighting.js:
- OR refitMask into fullMask per cascade, instead of turning any refit into shadowDirty for all.
- Per-cascade stale ceilings 12/24/60 frames. Sway is ~5 texels in c1 but about 1 texel in c2.

(3) shadow_caster_list.js: rasterise a FRUSTUM cascade as REFRESH (static pass, then depth blit to cache, then dynamic pass), so the cache is valid immediately (one extra blit).

(4) Receivers (materials.js _csmShadowFactor, terrain csmShadowFactor): select the cascade by length(worldPos - cameraPosition) against splits 30/100/300, not by view depth. Requires finding 2's world-position fix.

(5) Near/far per cascade: BACK_i at least radius_i plus a caster lead, and far = BACK_i + radius_i (see finding 7).

Optional follow-on: in c2 (64 cm texels), draw rigs as one instanced capsule proxy instead of their part meshes.

Ship behind ?csmStable, default on whenever ?csm=on.

findings.evidence:
The patch's world position skips the batching and instance transforms:
- materials.js:1461-1462: `vec4 _wp = modelMatrix * vec4(transformed, 1.0); vCsmWorldPos = _wp.xyz;`
- three r184 applies batchingMatrix and instanceMatrix after `transformed` (project_vertex.glsl.js; worldpos_vertex.glsl.js does it correctly). Cascade selection uses mvPosition, which is correct, but the lookup coordinate is not.

Batched variants carry the patch:
- batched_material_variant.js:128-140 mirrors every own property, onBeforeCompile included, onto the BatchedMesh variant.
- csm.js:284-288 confirms batched variants compile the CSM hook.

Affected receivers:
- buildings.js:369-370: building batches use instance matrix anchorInv*m.matrix, with receiveShadow from the template (387). buildingMatBatch has been default-on since 78e89aa5 (2026-10-17 19:49), after CSM went off (926f700a, 12:25 the same day), so it was never seen with shadows.
- static_batch_x.js:2381/2854: statics buckets use setMatrixAt(iid, m.matrix) and receiveShadow from the template.

findings.proposal:
In the vertex injection, mirror worldpos_vertex:

`vec4 _wp = vec4(transformed,1.0);`
`#ifdef USE_BATCHING _wp = batchingMatrix * _wp; #endif`
`#ifdef USE_INSTANCING _wp = instanceMatrix * _wp; #endif`
`_wp = modelMatrix * _wp;`

findings.title: The 3 intensity-0 cascade lights make every lit material run 3 dead RE_Direct + light-clamp blocks and 3 five-tap Vogel-PCF getShadow calls per fragment, and bloat every lit program

findings.evidence:
The cascade lights stay in every lit program:
- csm.js:224-226: cascade lights are DirectionalLight(intensity 0) with castShadow=true.
- WebGLLights.js:151-155 and 233 sort shadow casters first, so they are directional indices 0-2. NUM_DIR_LIGHTS goes from 2 to 5 (light_loops.js:20, '2 + 1 copies').

Each of them costs work that adds exactly zero:
- lights_fragment_begin.glsl.js:140-148: the directional loop is unrolled, and for i < NUM_DIR_LIGHT_SHADOWS calls getShadow before RE_Direct.
- shadowmap_pars_fragment.glsl.js:117-142: getShadow does an IGN hash plus 5 Vogel taps (sqrt/sin/cos plus a hardware compare each).
- The default-on light clamp wraps each RE_Direct copy (materials.js:2785-2847).
- The texture taps sit inside if(frustumTest) and a receiveShadow ternary, so ANGLE flattens them and they run unconditionally (same ANGLE mechanism round 1 confirmed for POM).
- Each lit program also holds 3 extra active sampler2DShadow units (directionalShadowMap[3]) bound to the same depth textures as the patch's own uCsm samplers.

The receiveShadow gating does nothing for CSM:
- materials.js:4264-4266: the CSM multiplier 'applies to every patched material whether or not the mesh receives shadows'.
- So receiveShadow feeds only this dead three path. The statics.js:230-245 rationale, tickShadowReceiveGate (loop.js:2662) and open:160 rest on a false premise.
findings.proposal:
On the CSM path only (at setupCsm, before any lit program with numDirLightShadows=3 compiles), rewrite THREE.ShaderChunk.lights_fragment_begin in the same fail-closed way as light_loops.js:
- Replace the exact head `#pragma unroll_loop_start\n\tfor ( int i = 0; i < NUM_DIR_LIGHTS; i ++ ) {\n\n\t\tdirectionalLight = directionalLights[ i ];` with `int i = NUM_DIR_LIGHT_SHADOWS;`.
- replaceLightNums turns it into digits before unrollLoops, so only indices 3-4 are emitted (verified with scratch dirloop_probe.mjs: anchor count 1, copies [3,4]).
- Optionally zero the shadowmap_vertex directional loop the same way.
- Escape: ?csmDeadLights=off. Never install it on ?shadows=on, where the sun is the caster.
- Afterwards, retire the receiveShadow distance gating; nothing reads it.

Rider (low confidence): at high/ultra the legacy setupSceneLighting sun is a permanent intensity-0 directional light (index.js:6431), which is one more dead RE_Direct per fragment. Removing it changes the light count, so do it only before first compile.
findings.expected_gain:

- 3 GGX + light-clamp evaluations

- 15 sin/cos pairs

That is roughly 300 ALU-equivalents plus 15 fetches against a ~300-600 ALU lit MeshStandard fragment. findings.title: CSM receiver taps are implicit-LOD texture() calls inside the cascade if-chain, so ANGLE/D3D11 flattens it and every fragment samples every cascade; textureLod(...,0.0) restores real branches
findings.evidence:
- materials.js:1400-1403: four `texture(sm, vec3(...))` taps per cascade.
- materials.js:1408-1440: a 6-way if/return chain picks the cascade (0, blend 0-1, 1, blend 1-2, 2, or beyond 300 m).
- terrain.js:2172-2207: the same structure, wrapped in `if (uCsmEnabled > 0.5)` (3720).
- An implicit-derivative sample inside control flow is a gradient op. ANGLE's HLSL metadata emits such ifs as [flatten] (the mechanism round-1 gpu-shading-1 confirmed for POM), so FXC evaluates all branches: up to 6 calls (≈12-24 compare taps plus 3-6 mat4 transforms per fragment) instead of 4 (8 in blend bands).
- The '>300 m skip' b249a762 relies on ('CSM: unchanged, already skipped past uCsmFar') is not a skip under FLATTEN.
- Shadow depth textures have no mips, so an explicit LOD 0 is identical.
findings.proposal: Replace each tap with `textureLod(sm, vec3(uv, ref), 0.0)`. GLSL ES 3.00 allows textureLod on sampler2DShadow, and ANGLE maps it to SampleCmpLevelZero. Do it in both the materials.js and terrain.js copies, hoisting nothing else. The if-chain then compiles to coherent dynamic branches: one cascade's 4 taps, 8 in the blend bands, none beyond uCsmFar. Bump the program key and add an escape ?csmLod0=off.
findings.expected_gain: Shadow taps drop from ~12-24 to 4-8 per receiver fragment. Basis: the 10-17 one-feature-off A/B priced terrain shadow sampling at −0.85 ms GPU (ultra 1070), and receivers on buildings and statics add to that. Estimated 0.3-1.2 ms GPU at ultra with CSM on. It depends on how much FXC CSE already merges the duplicated calls, so it is unmeasured.
findings.novelty_check: Not in ledger or corrected.md. Round-1 gpu-shading-1 is the same ANGLE flatten mechanism applied to POM only. The terrainFarSimplify commit message assumed the CSM skip was real.
findings.verify_how: On the 1070, dump the translated HLSL with WEBGL_debug_shaders for the terrain and one MeshStandard receiver, before and after, and look for FLATTEN and SampleCmp vs SampleCmpLevelZero. Then run a GPU timer A/B on the terrain draw with ?csm=on. On the laptop, a pixel-diff of a parked frame must be identical.

findings.title: Shadow depth pass re-resolves programs on draw-kind changes: three's single shared depth material flips between batched, instanced and plain casters, and the shared sway depth material also flips on alphaTest. Sorting the caster list by depth-program kind removes it
findings.evidence:
Where the shadow pass picks its depth material:
- three r184 WebGLShadowMap.getDepthMaterial (WebGLShadowMap.js:418-482) hands every opaque, non-alpha-tested caster the one shared _depthMaterial.
- Alpha-tested casters get per-material clones (441-462).
- Swaying casters all share swayDepthMaterial (sway_shadow.js:53-79), with alphaTest and map written onto it per draw (480-482).

What a flip costs:
- WebGLRenderer.js:2392-2414: a material object switching between BatchedMesh, InstancedMesh and plain Mesh (and between colour and no-colour variants) sets needsProgramChange.
- Material.js:493-503: alphaTest crossing 0 bumps version, which also forces a change.
- Each flip re-runs getParameters and getProgramCacheKey, swaps currentProgram and rebuilds the uniform list: ~20-30 µs (repo figures of 16-19 µs per re-resolve plus the list rebuild).
- batched_material_variant.js documents the same flip for the colour pass and fixes it there only.

Why flips are frequent here:
- The candidate list is in scene-graph DFS order, so per-LB groups interleave batches, singletons and instanced statics, and sway buckets interleave bark (alphaTest 0) with ClipMap leaves (alphaTest 100/255).
- 68 of 128 submitted statics batches at Nanto are sway (statics.js:2541-2544).
- This plausibly explains why a shadow draw measured ~31 µs of submission (12.1 ms / 390, interior_shadow_cull.js:12-14), more than colour draws.
- shadow_caster_list.js's own header states depth-only draws are order-free.
findings.proposal:
(1) In collect / collectSplit (and on the dynamic list), stable-sort the candidates by depth-program kind before handing them to three:
- key = (customDepthMaterial id, isBatchedMesh, colorTexture != null, isInstancedMesh, instanceColor != null, alphaTest > 0 && (map || alphaMap), side).
- It is pixel-identical: depth min is order-independent and receivers read only the depthTexture.

(2) sway_shadow.js: build the sway depth material once per alphaTest class (cutout / solid) and pick it in applySwayShadow from obj.material.alphaTest. Re-check it in collect, which already touches every caster, so a fade flip re-picks.

(3) Add a counter of needsProgramChange inside shadow rasters, exposed on __shadowCasterList.stats.
findings.expected_gain: Flips per light drop from O(kind transitions in DFS order) to at most ~6. Unmeasured: if 30-50% of the ~390 draws in a full 3-cascade raster flip at ~25 µs, that is ~3-5 ms of the ~12 ms raster. Under finding 1 it applies to each REFRESH/overlay rather than every frame, so the steady-state value is ~0.2-1 ms/frame.
findings.novelty_check: Advances ledger-open:159 (sway alphaTest version bumps, 'unmeasured'). It adds the concrete three r184 lines, generalises the problem to three's own shared _depthMaterial batched/instanced/plain flips (not in any ledger), gives an S-effort fix inside the existing wrapper, and adds a counter so it can be priced. batched_material_variant covers the colour pass only.

Pixel-diff the shadow maps by reading back the depthTexture for one raster: identical. On the 1070: main-thread ms per raster frame from __shadowScope stats plus a profile.

findings.title: Fixed NDC bias over a 434-725 m light depth range leaks 0.3-0.5 m of light at every contact, and c2's sun-side cap falls outside the depth range
findings.evidence:
How big the bias is in world terms:
- csm.js:79 BACK_DIST_M=200; csm.js:765-766 near=0.1, far = BACK_DIST_M*2 + radius.
- The receivers use a constant `bias = 0.0007` in [0,1] depth (materials.js:1392, terrain.js:2172).
- At the default retail FOV (53.6° vertical, scratch csm_radii.mjs) that is 0.30 / 0.36 / 0.51 m along the light ray for c0/c1/c2, against texels of 3.4 / 10.6 / 63.5 cm. About 9 texels of bias in c0.
- Receivers within ~0.3 m of the occluder along the ray read lit: a ~0.26 m lit strip along the base of every wall in its own shadow at 30° sun, and detached shadows under feet.
- three already renders BackSide for FrontSide casters (WebGLShadowMap.js:51), so closed meshes need little bias.

Dead config and a clipped cap:
- light.shadow.bias / normalBias (csm.js:230-231) feed only three's dead getShadow (finding 3).
- c2's radius (~325 m) exceeds BACK_DIST_M, so the sphere's sun-side cap (light depth < 0) lies in front of the near plane. There, casters are not rasterised and receivers return lit.
findings.proposal:
Per cascade:
- BACK_i = max(radius_i + lead, 200), where lead is about H_max / sin(elevation), capped.
- far_i = BACK_i + radius_i. The extra BACK beyond the sphere covers no receiver.
- Bias uniform uCsmBias[i] = k·texel_i / range_i (k ≈ 1.5-2).
- A small normal offset along the geometry normal for DoubleSide foliage, reusing the configured normalBias.

Escape: ?csmBias=legacy.
findings.expected_gain: Visual: contact shadows reattach, removing the lit seam at wall bases and floating feet, and far-cascade shadows return in the sun-side cap. No fps change. A tighter range also improves depth precision.
findings.novelty_check: Not in ledger or corrected.md. Round-1 recent-render-diff-2 covers three's PCF bias SIGN on ?shadows=on, a different path; this is the custom CSM receivers' magnitude and range. Searched bias, peter, acne, leak.

findings.title: Rigs culled from the main camera (frustum, occlusion, cell gate) also vanish from the shadow maps, so long rig shadows pop at the screen edge at low sun and for large creatures
findings.evidence:
How a culled rig loses its shadow:
- entities.js:3075 ENTITY_CULL_RADIUS=6; 3250 culler.isSphereInFrustum against the main camera. The occlusionCull and rigCellGate paths (3255-3283) also set _renderCullHidden.
- _applyEntityVisible (3023-3028) writes root.visible=false.
- shadow_caster_list.js:94/114 collect skips visible===false subtrees, as does three's renderObject (WebGLShadowMap.js renderObject `if (object.visible === false) return`).
- lighting.js's mover-scope comment confirms a hidden rig 'puts nothing in any shadow map'.

When it shows: a shadow of length h/tan(e) leaves the 6 m pad when e < ~17° for a 1.8 m human, and at e < 34-53° for 4-8 m creatures. Shadows of rigs beside or behind the camera then pop in and out on screen as it turns.
findings.proposal:
With CSM live:
- In the render cull, test a second sphere centred at root + shadowDirFlat·L/2 with radius 6 + L/2, where L = min(h_max/tan(e), uCsmFar).
- Rigs that pass only this test become shadow-only. Keep them out of the main pass and add them to the dynamic shadow list in shadowStaticCacheRender: set root.visible=true for the pass and call updateWorldMatrix first, since ?skipHiddenMatrix freezes them.
- Fade to nothing via finding 5's strength.

Flag: ?csmOffscreenCasters.
findings.expected_gain: Visual: no shadow pop at frustum edges. Cost: matrix updates plus depth draws for a handful of extra rigs, mostly only at low sun.
findings.novelty_check: Not in ledger or corrected.md. Searched off-screen, pop, hidden rig, frustum cull with shadow. The mover-scope comment records the behaviour as intended for perf, not as a visual issue.

refutes.reasons:
I could not refute the shader bug itself, but the list of affected receivers is wrong.

What holds:
- materials.js:1458-1462 injects `vec4 _wp = modelMatrix * vec4(transformed, 1.0); vCsmWorldPos = _wp.xyz;` right after `#include <project_vertex>`.
- In three r184 (node_modules/three 0.184.0), both project_vertex and worldpos_vertex apply batchingMatrix and then instanceMatrix to `transformed`, so `transformed` includes neither.
- vCsmWorldPos has no other writer, and no other patch rewrites project_vertex first.
- batchingMatrix is declared by batching_vertex, which comes before project_vertex (meshphysical lines 31 and 44), so the proposed fix compiles.
- Receivers really do carry the patch:
  - statics.js:3126 calls `materialCache.getCached(did)`, which returns the base (doubleSided defaults to true). MaterialCache:5319 puts the CSM hook on the base when csmState exists.
  - `?staticBatch` (always-on) and `?statBatchChunk` (default-on) feed groups of 2 or more into static_batch_x.js buckets. Each bucket draws `batchedMaterialFor(mat)`, whose own-key mirror copies onBeforeCompile and customProgramCacheKey.
  - Those buckets use staticsGroup-relative `setMatrixAt(iid, m.matrix)` (static_batch_x.js:2854). So under `?csm=on` their lookups land near the world origin, outside every cascade, and `_csmSampleCascade` returns 1.0. Repeated-material statics are therefore never shadowed.

What is wrong:
1. Building shells are not affected today. On the default `?buildingFloorBias` arm, buildings.js:896-898 draws the floor-bias clone (`getCachedFloorBias` = `base.clone()` + `applyFloorDepthBias`). The building batch batches that clone (buildings.js header: "share a material OBJECT (the per-DID floor-bias clone)"). three's Material.copy does not copy onBeforeCompile; a node probe confirmed the clone keeps the prototype no-op. The clone has no CSM hook at all, which is open:11. The new buildingMatBatch matrices therefore change nothing visible, and the proposed fix alone gives building walls nothing. The "garbage patches on building walls" case (an LB-corner-anchored lookup) only happens on `?buildingFloorBias=off`.
2. Atlas buckets (static_atlas.js makeArrayMaterial = new MeshStandardMaterial; the file has no csm code) carry no CSM patch either. The 17,774-instance figure includes atlas and building buckets, so it overstates how many receivers this fix affects.
3. The statics.js:2232/2243 InstancedMesh walk-in path is opt-in (`walkInInstance` defaults to false). Only the ring-baker InstancedMesh use may be live.
4. verify_how is off target. It reads vCsmWorldPos on "one building batch", but that program has no such varying, and it eye-tests building walls, which this fix does not touch. The program-key bump is unnecessary because programs do not persist across page loads; it is harmless.

None of this shows on the default URL: CSM is off on every tier.

The atlas buckets also have no CSM. So for building walls (the 1070 eye-test target) the proposed fix changes nothing until open:11 is fixed too. The CSM receiver patch (materials.js:1461) builds vCsmWorldPos without batchingMatrix or instanceMatrix. Every receiver that actually carries the patch and draws as a BatchedMesh or InstancedMesh samples cascades at the wrong place. Today that means:

findings.evidence:

Boot grace: bootGraceActive (:132-139) keys on the FIRST 'ready' (history.find) and is the only isBooting input (index.js:1498-1500). So teleports, portals and LB-crossing bursts after ready+30 s are unprotected.

findings.title: 3D canvas inherits the legacy 2D rule `image-rendering: pixelated`, so any render scale below 1 is upscaled nearest-neighbour by the compositor
findings.area: index.html canvas CSS / scene3d render-scale path
findings.evidence:
index.html:160 sets `#stage canvas { border: 1px solid #ccc; background:#101010; image-rendering: pixelated; cursor: grab; }`. It came from the Phase-3 2D pixel-art page (git -S: f04b1f5f); the 2D/Pixi path was retired 2026-06-20.

The 3D canvas (index.html:954) sits inside #stage. The agent-mode override (index.html:498-502) changes size, display and outline but neither image-rendering nor border.

The film tooling's own recon confirms the live state: clean_frame.js:7-9 says the canvas keeps 'border:1px solid #ccc; image-rendering:pixelated … supersampled buffers are downscaled nearest-neighbour'. It fixes this only for film (clean_frame.js:56-57: image-rendering:auto, border:0).

The render scale sets the drawing buffer through setPixelRatio(min(DPR,2)×scale) plus setSize(...,false) with CSS untouched (index.js:1436, 1449-1454). So whenever scale<1 (FP-1's 0.88/0.76 lowers, FP-5's 0.84 1440p default) or DPR>2, the compositor upscales with nearest-neighbour. At 0.88 that duplicates every ~8th row and column, which crawls as the camera moves, rather than giving a uniform bilinear softness. The 1 px #ccc border is also visible on the top and left edges of the agent-mode view and offsets the content by 1 CSS px (fractional at DPR 1.25).
findings.proposal:
Add `#stage canvas#canvas { image-rendering: auto; border: 0; }`, or set both in preInit3D for the 3D path (HUD-class CSS, apply direct). This matches what film mode already applies.

Optional follow-up, needs-eyetest: when renderScale<1, upscale inside the final post pass (bilinear plus a light CAS-style sharpen) instead of in the compositor.

Visual only, with zero cost. Output is pixel-identical at a 1:1 buffer (the owner's 1080p scale-1 case). At any scale below 1 or DPR above 2, the irregular nearest-neighbour stair pattern gives way to uniform filtering, and the stray 1 px grey frame disappears.

- computeInitialRenderScale (adaptive_render_scale.js:215-231) caps device pixels at pixelBudget 2.6 Mpx (:222) regardless of DPR. index.js:1425-1436 applies it when there is no explicit renderScale. The agent-mode cap is 4096 (index.js:938).

Its main consequence is that those raises arm FP-1's settle window. The owner's documented 1080p sessions are unaffected.

Applying the budget only at basePixelRatio >= 1.5, or raising it to ~3.7 Mpx, is a cheap correctness tweak with a unit test. It is low value.

findings.title: Fade funnel: faded entity parts are drawn twice per frame (with two forced program re-resolves), and at opacity 0 they are still drawn — fix all three gaps in syncFadeAlpha
findings.area: scene3d/fade_alpha_state.js syncFadeAlpha / restoreAuthoredAlpha (the funnel all four fade owners call)
findings.evidence:
Single-pass flag is never set on fades:
- applyRetailSinglePass returns early unless `mat.transparent===true` at build time (materials.js:2073-2080), and it only runs at build.
- syncFadeAlpha's faded arm (fade_alpha_state.js:94-112) sets transparent=true and depthWrite=false but never touches forceSinglePass.
- So every faded opaque DoubleSide entity part (all entity materials are DoubleSide, entities.js:6856-6869) hits three r184's renderObject two-pass: BackSide then FrontSide, each preceded by `material.needsUpdate = true` (three.module.js:18065-18074).
- The repo's own 1070 A/B priced that path at ~66 us per extra draw, CPU-side (url-flags.md:391, 15.7 ms over 236 draws).

Who fades (all four owners funnel through syncFadeAlpha: entities.js:19171/19318/19412/19593):
- camera near-fade and in-head view (_applyCamFadeToInst, entities.js:19562; retailCamZoom default-ON camera.js:612; in-head pushes opacity 0.0 every frame, camera.js:2059);
- object translucency (entities.js:19366);
- Transparent hook ramps.

Opacity-0 parts are still drawn: in first person every part of the local player (and its held items, via camFadeHier) sits at opacity 0 and is drawn twice invisibly every frame. Retail skips the part entirely at translucency 1.0 (CPhysicsPart::SetTranslucency `draw_state |= 1`, acclient.c:315497-315503).

Hidden third bug (lead 7): three keys `#define OPAQUE` on `transparent` (three.module.js:7634), and setProgram never re-checks transparent (three.module.js:18316-18430). Today the two-pass needsUpdate churn accidentally refreshes it. Setting forceSinglePass alone, without a version bump, would unmask lead 7: faded parts would render at alpha 1.
findings.proposal:
In syncFadeAlpha's faded arm:
(a) If `mat.side===DoubleSide && surfaceSinglePassEnabled()`, record the authored forceSinglePass in `__authoredAlpha`, set it true, and set `mat.needsUpdate=true` once. That bump also refreshes the OPAQUE define, closing lead 7.
(b) If `opacity<=0 && blending===NormalBlending && depthWrite===false` (materialRendersNothing's first four clauses, re-derived on every owner write), set `mat.visible=false` (authored value recorded). Clear it when the opacity rises. Gate (b) on `!csmEnabled && !shadowsEnabled`, because material.visible also drops the shadow cast and the first-person self-shadow is an owner call (ledger-compact 48).

In restoreAuthoredAlpha:
- put back forceSinglePass and visible;
- bump needsUpdate when transparent returns to its authored false, so the part goes back onto the exact OPAQUE program its never-faded peers use.

Ship behind ?fadeSinglePass (default-on, =off escape). Material.visible is per-entity safe: _getOrCloneEntityMaterial always hands out private clones (entities.js:15093-15160).

Based on the 1070-measured ~66 us per extra two-pass draw (url-flags.md:391).

Mesh counts are estimated, not counted.

findings.title: buildNraArray fills every atlas NRA array with a scalar 4-byte loop (and grow fills the whole new array, then overwrites the copied prefix): use Uint32Array.fill and fill only the tail
findings.evidence:
static_atlas.js:366-373 writes data[i..i+3] for every texel of w*h*layers.

Sizes: x4 BC7 buckets carry RGBA8 NRA at the BC7 dims (static_atlas.js:1222-1225, :1265-1279).
- 1024² buckets: 4 MiB per layer;
- 2048² buckets: 16 MiB per layer, with a capacity floor of 4, so 64 MB arrays.
Armed statAtlasPages opens new pages at the X7 depths (url-flags.md:797), so every new page or bucket pays the fill on the main thread.

The grow path (static_atlas.js:1489-1494) calls buildNraArray for the whole target depth and then `.set()`s the live prefix over it, so about two-thirds of the fill is wasted. adapter.js:1742-1752 does the same scalar fill for the 33-layer terrain PBR NRA at boot.

Node bench (nra_fill_bench.mjs, laptop, allocation included in both arms):
- 32 MB: 97.1 ms → 20.9 ms;
- 64 MB: 198.9 ms → 40.6 ms;
- 128 MB: 236 ms → 86 ms.
Bytes identical (checked).
findings.proposal:
Replace the loop with a single fill: `new Uint32Array(data.buffer, data.byteOffset, len>>>2).fill((A<<24|R<<16|N<<8|N)>>>0)`. Add a little-endian guard and fall back to the loop on big-endian (never on x86/ARM browsers).
Give buildNraArray an optional `fillFromLayer` argument so _growBucketLayers fills only [allocLayers, target).
Apply the same change to buildPbrNraTexture and to static_array_pool's use of buildNraArray.
findings.expected_gain: Byte-identical. About 4-5x less main-thread time per NRA allocation: tens to about 160 ms saved per new 2048² page on the laptop, roughly half that on the 1070 desktop (assumed). On grows about 10x, because the prefix is no longer filled twice. Roughly 70 ms one-off at boot for a 512-tile terrain NRA. Complements round-1 memory-1, which shrinks the arrays themselves.
findings.novelty_check: Advances ledger-open 278 ('Chunk atlas grow / replace buildNraArray scalar per-texel fill — modelled 20-250 ms per grow, never measured'). It adds the measured cost, the exact byte-identical replacement, the wasted prefix fill on grow, and the second boot site in adapter.js. Round-1 memory-1 sized NRA but did not touch the fill.

findings.title: Atlas BC7 statics sample level 0 with no mips at every distance; the only real blocker to giving them mips is three r184 clearing layerUpdates after mip 0, which a per-texture override fixes exactly
findings.area: scene3d/static_atlas.js _getOrCreateBucket; scene3d/bc7_textures.js makeBc7ArrayTexture / writeBc7ArrayLayer; bc7 singleton buildAndSwap
findings.evidence:
Default arm (texCompressedOnly off, bc7_textures.js:213-223): BC7 atlas arrays are allocated level-0-only with `{}` (static_atlas.js:1316-1325), which forces LinearFilter (bc7_textures.js:784-822). Every distant atlas static therefore samples a 1024²/2048² level 0: aliasing, plus texture-cache-hostile fetches on a fill-bound 1070.

What is already in place:
- The payloads carry full chains (bc7_textures.js:22-29).
- The wrap shader is mip-ready: textureGrad with unwrapped derivatives (static_atlas.js:617-635).
- Pages and grows already copy every level of chain arrays (static_atlas.js:1478-1487).

The remaining cost is three's upload loop: it uploads marked layers at mip 0, calls clearLayerUpdates() inside the mip loop, and then uploads the FULL depth at every level 1+ (three.module.js:12046-12066). That is about a third of the array per layer write, and bc7_textures.js:43-47 documents it as 'restructured by ST9'.

Separately, the singleton swap passes no anisotropy (bc7_textures.js:2094-2100), so a swapped texture drops from adapter aniso to 1.
findings.proposal:
(1) Pixel-identical upload fix on chain arrays: replace the texture's clearLayerUpdates with a no-op, and chain `onUpdate` (three calls it at the end of uploadTexture, three.module.js:12378; chaining as at bc7_textures.js:504-510) to clear layerUpdates after all levels. Each write then uploads only the marked layers at every level. Unmarked layers held identical bytes, so skipping them changes nothing.
(2) A new default-off `?atlasBc7Mips` flag, decoupled from texCompressedOnly's PVW/controller preconditions, that passes `{mipChain:true, anisotropy:getAdapterMaxAnisotropy()}` at static_atlas.js:1316-1325.
(3) A one-line `anisotropy: old?.anisotropy` in buildAndSwap, behind the same eye test.
findings.expected_gain:
(1) Chain-array layer writes go from about array/3 bytes to 4/3 of one layer, about 10-20x less upload per write for 6-16-layer buckets. It removes the stated blocker.
(2) Distant atlas statics stop shimmering, a certain visual improvement. GPU effect is likely net positive at distance (mip-cache locality), but aniso adds cost, so the sign is for the 1070 to decide. Memory: +1/3 on BC7 atlas diffuse, about +40-50 MB heap and VRAM at Nanto-class sites, offset many times over if round-1 memory-1 lands.
findings.novelty_check: Advances ledger-open 328/281 (atlas BC7 level-0-only, singleton aniso drop; 'orchestrator call never made') and 363 (chain writes upload full depth at mips 1+, deferred to ST9). findings.title: The unanchored instanced-statics THREE.LOD is not on the default path at all (buildInstancedNode only runs under the declined ?walkInInstance); where it does run it always draws the deepest band, and url-flags misstates why
findings.area: scene3d/statics.js buildInstancedNode, bakeStaticsRing; docs/url-flags.md walkInInstance row
findings.evidence:
buildInstancedNode builds `new THREE.LOD()` with no position, and instance matrices carry world coordinates (statics.js:2276-2278, :2230-2240). three r184 LOD.update measures camera-to-LOD matrixWorld distance (three.core.js:21803 class, update at +218..256). staticsGroup is an identity Group (index.js:1739), so the distance is the camera's distance from the map origin: about 47 km at Holtburg, where (0xA9·192, 0xB4·192) ≈ (32.4 km, 34.6 km). Every instanced LOD therefore shows its LAST level at all distances.

This never runs by default:
- The only callers are bakeStaticsRing (statics.js:3990), which has no production caller (statics.js:4229-4231; rg finds no call outside tests);
- and the walk-in pass 2 (statics.js:3185-3200), gated by walkInInstanceEnabled, which is opt-in (`=== on`, statics.js:2480-2490) and declined by owner directive (url-flags.md:837; ledger-compact 649).
The url-flags row attributes the instanced LOD trade to 'picks ONE level per node from the node centre', but the node sits at the world origin, so the band is always the deepest.
findings.proposal: Close lead 1 as latent: no default-path cost or look impact today. Correct the url-flags walkInInstance row: deepest band at all distances, not a node-centre pick. If walkInInstance is ever revisited, its per-LB nodes need either an LOD anchored at the group's bounding-sphere centre (subtract the anchor from instance matrices), or no LOD wrapper, keeping chained models on the singleton path. The 'unknown how much of the default path uses this node' question in lead 1 is answered: none.

findings.title: Sky-object particle chains are attached once and never detached: storm-window chains (0x33000428/42C/453) keep running after the window closes, the DayGroup changes or weather is turned off
findings.evidence:
scene3d/sky_dome.js:550-604 updateSkyParticleChains attaches each visible pesObjectId once. The guard set is filled at :590-591 and only cleared in dispose() at :777-789. Objects that become invisible (`if (pes === 0 || !vis) continue`) or vanish from the snapshot are never detached.

skyBirds is default ON (url-flags.md:1010, `!== "off"`). It is called every sky tick from scene3d/loop.js:1597, after the weather-off filter at :1569-1570, so turning on 'Disable most weather effects' mid-session only stops new attaches.

crates/holtburger-world/src/sky.rs:117-120: the props=0x0D storm SetupModels carry PES 0x33000428/42C/453 and ALL have windowed begin/end (76 occurrences across the 20 DayGroups). The 0x320002C2 lightning box is drawn in its legacy look (sky_glow.js:56; particle-fx-catalog: 'a 2 km additive solid box lit for one frame', looped by CallPES).

Retail destroys these objects:
- SkyDesc::GetSky (acclient.c:302962-303030) gives an out-of-window object a null gfx_id.
- GameSky::CreateDeletePhysicsObjects (acclient.c:308687+) deletes every sky CPhysicsObj whose data id or properties no longer match the DayGroup's list, or when the weather option flips. That also drops its particles and scripts.

Why a plain owner reap is not enough: the chain's CallPES loop is guarded only by anchor.userData.__scriptEpoch and anchor.parent (statics.js:5757-5765). All sky chains share the one _skyBirdAnchor. So ownerRegistry.destroyAllForOwner('sky:'+pes) (owner_registry.js:503) kills the live emitters, but the next CallPES tick re-creates them under the new owner epoch.
findings.proposal:
Give each PES its own child anchor and reap it when it is no longer wanted.
- Child anchor: `sub = new THREE.Group()`, with `sub.userData.isSkyGlowAnchor = true` so statics.js:5806 skyGlow tagging still works. Add it under _skyBirdAnchor (camera-follow is inherited) and keep it in a `_skyChainAnchors` Map(pes → sub). Attach the chain to `sub`.
- Each tick, with a non-null snapshot array, build `want` = the set of visible PES ids, empty when the array is empty.
- For every attached pes not in `want`: bump `sub.userData.__scriptEpoch`, `sub.parent.remove(sub)`, call `ownerRegistry.destroyAllForOwner('sky:'+pes)`, and delete the pes from both maps.
- The epoch bump plus the detach stops pending CallPES and deferred hook timers (statics.js:5757-5765, _scheduleStaticCreate). In-flight creates self-destroy through the owner epoch (owner_registry.js:504-506) and the post-create anchor-epoch check (statics.js:5823-5827).
- A null snapshot (the wasm call failed) keeps everything (fail open).
- dispose() is unchanged.
- Add an escape `?skyChainLifecycle=off`.
- Optional retail nicety: key per sky-object index, not per PES, so overlapping objects sharing a PES each get a chain as in retail. Not required.
findings.expected_gain: Correctness/visual. After the first storm window of a session (a Dereth day is 7620 s, so most sessions longer than ~2 h, and any login inside a storm window), storm chains currently run until page reload: lightning-box flashes on fair days and after disabling weather. They also tick on the shared static particle manager forever (a small CPU leak, a few emitters plus a CallPES loop). The fix restores retail's per-window lifetime. It has no cost.

findings.title: The vivid-targeting off-screen arrow points back toward the screen centre instead of at the target (a +180° slip)
findings.evidence:
scene3d/selection_brackets.js:825-837 builds the arrow as a CSS triangle (border-bottom solid, left and right transparent), which points UP.

_showOffScreen (:1047-1080) places it at the viewport edge along the target's screen direction: px = halfW + nx·s, py = halfH − ny·s. It then rotates by `deg = atan2(nx, ny)·180/π + 180` (:1074).
