refutes.reasons:
I could not refute the claim. Every citation checks out against current source, and both failure modes follow from the code plus Chrome's Windows event order.

Citations checked:
- camera.js:963-971: on a right press on the canvas it calls `getInputFunnel().noteCanvasRightPress()` at :970 and calls preventDefault on the mousedown.
- The canvas contextmenu handler (:959-962, attached :1067) only calls preventDefault.
- onMouseUp is a document listener (:1073). It handles a right click that moved less than 5 px over a picked entity (:1032) and calls `window.__openContextMenuFor` (:1039-1045).
- Follow is the default camera mode (camera.js:460).
- radial-menu is in plugins/index.json and loads by default. Its line 859 is the only place `__openContextMenuFor` is defined; nothing overrides it.
- openContextMenuFor (:600-752) is fully synchronous:
  - it appends the overlay;
  - `placeAt` (:224) puts it at pointer +2/+2 HUD px, or flips it away from the pointer at screen edges;
  - it then adds `document.addEventListener("contextmenu", state.onContextMenu, true)` (:751);
  - that handler (:743-748) calls closeMenu() for any target outside the overlay or submenu.
- The radial listener and the camera mouseup opener have both been there since 09b13f93; there was never a deferral.

Why each case fails on Windows:
- The funnel uses the canvas mark only in a document listener in the bubble phase (input-funnel.js:674-684), and only when `?nativeContextMenu` is off. It clears the mark in a capture-phase mousedown (:672).
- Bubble phase means it runs after every element handler. The comment at :687-693 says so itself, and so does the input-options-8 follow-up in fu3.txt.
- Chrome on Windows (ShowContextMenuOnMouseUp) dispatches contextmenu right after the mouseup handlers, to the element under the pointer.
- Case (b), menu opens and closes in one click: by the time contextmenu fires, the radial capture listener is live. The target is the canvas, outside the off-pointer overlay, so the menu closes in the same gesture.
- Case (a), camera turn released over the HUD: the target is the HUD cell, and its own handler runs.
  - combat-bar.js:1450-1453 calls clearCell() → setSpellBarSlot(i, 0).
  - map-panel.js:1368-1371 clears the waypoint.
  - hotbar.js:1440 opens the item menu.
  - The inventory, container and corpse cells do the same.
- No existing mechanism stops either path. No capture-phase contextmenu listener exists other than the radial one, and no cell checks the canvas mark.

The proposed fix works:
- A window capture listener runs before the document capture listener, so stopImmediatePropagation pre-empts both radial-menu.js:751 and the element handlers.
- On Linux the swallow happens at mousedown, before any menu exists, so it does no harm there.
- Rendering is pixel-identical.
refutes.strongest_counterargument:
The Windows behaviour is inferred, not seen.
- It comes from Chromium's Windows contextmenu-on-mouseup ordering (and the project's own input-options-8 comments, which came from a code comparison with WebAC, not a Windows bug report). Nobody has run it on a Windows machine.
- The radial menu has behaved this way since May (09b13f93), and no Windows report of 'right-click menu flashes and closes' exists in the ledgers or git. That is surprising for a break this complete. The likeliest reason is that nobody has right-clicked 3D entities on Windows on-screen (1070 tests are headless or batched), not that the bug is absent.
- Chrome's HandleMouseUp → MouseContextMenu path is well documented, and the code path is fully synchronous, so I found no mechanism that would save the menu. One small exception: placeAt clamping could cover the pointer when the menu is taller than the viewport, which is an edge case.

Two minor points on the proposal:
- The `_onAnyPress` mark reset is only installed when `nativeContextMenu` is off, so the new listener must go in that block or get its own reset.
- The `?canvasCtxSwallow=off` flag is optional under the HUD rule.

Impact 'high' holds only on Windows. Linux and macOS are unaffected.
refutes.residual_claim:
Holds as stated, inferred from source and Chrome's Windows event order rather than seen on a Windows machine.

Root cause: on Windows, contextmenu fires after mouseup at whatever is under the release point. The canvas-press mark is used only by the funnel's bubble-phase document listener, which runs after element handlers. Two results:
- (a) A camera right-drag released over the HUD runs that cell's own contextmenu handler. Spell-bar slots get cleared (combat-bar.js:1450-1453), the map waypoint gets cleared (map-panel.js:1368-1371), and hotbar, inventory, container and corpse cells pop item menus.
- (b) A short right-click on a 3D entity opens the radial menu synchronously on mouseup (camera.js:1032-1045 → radial-menu.js:600). The menu's own capture-phase contextmenu listener (:751) sees the following contextmenu targeted at the canvas, outside the overlay placed at pointer +2/+2, and closes the menu in the same gesture (:743-748).

Fix: a window capture contextmenu listener that calls preventDefault and stopImmediatePropagation and consumes `_rightPressOnCanvas`. Install it with or alongside the `_onAnyPress` mousedown reset. Rendering is pixel-identical, there is no effect on Linux or macOS, and one on-screen Windows check is still owed.
